title: Trump Bombs Houthi Targets in Yemen Amid Signal Chat Scandal
description_short: Trump Bombs Houthi Targets in Yemen Amid Signal Chat Scandal
description_medium: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration launched strikes against Houthi targets in Yemen, citing attacks on Red Sea shipping. That week, senior officials discussed the operation in a Signal group chat that inadvertently included The Atlantic editor Jeffrey Goldberg. Reuters reported that the chat concerned strike coordination, while the administration disputed that classified information had been shared. The disclosure drew scrutiny to operational security and oversight.
description_long: The Trump administration began airstrikes against Houthi targets in Yemen on March 15, 2025, describing them as a response to attacks on shipping in the Red Sea. During the same week, senior officials used a Signal group chat to discuss the operation. National Security Adviser Mike Waltz, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Vice President J.D. Vance were among the officials in the conversation. The Atlantic editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg was inadvertently added and saw messages about the strikes before they began. Reuters reported that the chat concerned coordination of the Yemen operation. The administration disputed that classified information had been shared, while the accidental inclusion of a journalist prompted questions about how officials protected sensitive military discussions. The chat’s timing made its security especially consequential: it concerned an active operation rather than a routine policy debate. The episode drew attention to the government’s use of a consumer messaging service for national-security communications and to the controls governing who could access those discussions.

title: Donald Trump: The United States won't make it to 2104
description_short: Donald Trump: The United States won't make it to 2104
description_medium: In an interview published in Playboy’s October 2004 issue, Donald Trump said he did not expect the United States as then known to exist a century later. Asked whether his buildings would still bear his name, he replied that he doubted any building would remain. He pointed to powerful weapons and wider access to them, though the exact interview date is unknown.
description_long: Donald Trump spoke with Playboy sometime before its October 2004 issue, although the interview’s exact date is unknown. Asked whether Trump Tower and his other buildings would still bear his name a hundred years later, he said he doubted any building would remain. He linked the prediction to the growing danger of powerful weapons and the ease of obtaining them, saying the world would not be the same unless “very smart people” entered office quickly. When the interviewer called the thought frightening, Trump replied that the world was rocky and terrible things would happen. The exchange came while Trump was discussing his buildings and the possibility that they would carry his name far into the future. His answer shifted from the fate of his real estate to the possibility that global conflict could leave no buildings standing. He described a bleak future but did not name a particular weapon or propose a specific policy response. The interview captures his public comments on nuclear danger and access to powerful weapons before he entered presidential politics.

title: Trump: Giuliani & pedophile hold campaign event at a landscaping company
description_short: Trump: Giuliani & pedophile hold campaign event at a landscaping company
description_medium: On November 7, 2020, Rudy Giuliani held a Trump campaign press conference at Four Seasons Total Landscaping in Philadelphia while challenging the election result. Corey Lewandowski, Pam Bondi and Daryl Brooks were also present. Brooks claimed to be a local poll watcher, though reporting said he lived elsewhere and had prior sex-offense convictions. News outlets had just called the race for Joe Biden as reporters began leaving.
description_long: Rudy Giuliani held a press conference for the Trump campaign at Four Seasons Total Landscaping in Philadelphia on November 7, 2020. Campaign adviser Corey Lewandowski, Pam Bondi and Daryl Brooks joined him. Brooks presented himself as a Philadelphia poll watcher, but reporting said he did not live in the city and had been incarcerated in the 1990s for offenses involving sexual assault, lewdness and endangering a minor. Trenton Mayor Reed Gusciora recognized Brooks as a New Jersey political candidate and questioned Giuliani’s description of him as a Philadelphia resident and poll watcher. The campaign used the event to repeat claims of widespread voter fraud as major news outlets called the presidential race for Joe Biden. Reporters began packing up while Giuliani was speaking, and the unusual location quickly became part of the story. Brooks’s claimed role drew additional scrutiny because his residence and election credentials were disputed. The event took place as the campaign continued its effort to challenge the result, even after Biden had been projected as the winner.

title: Jan 6 Rally: Trump Directs Crowd to March to Capitol While Pence Refuses
description_short: Jan 6 Rally: Trump Directs Crowd to March to Capitol While Pence Refuses
description_medium: On January 6, 2021, Donald Trump told supporters gathered near the White House to march to the Capitol while Congress counted the electoral votes. He falsely claimed the election had been stolen and knew Vice President Mike Pence would not block certification. The House January 6 committee concluded that the speech was part of a coordinated effort to use the crowd to pressure Pence and Congress.
description_long: On January 6, 2021, President Donald Trump spoke to thousands of supporters at the Ellipse near the White House as Congress prepared to certify the 2020 election. He repeated false claims that the election had been stolen and urged the crowd to march to the Capitol, saying he would go with them, though he did not. Before the speech, Vice President Mike Pence had told Trump he would not block certification of Joe Biden’s electoral votes; Trump had also pressured Pence by phone and in public messages. The House Select Committee investigating January 6 concluded that the speech formed part of a coordinated plan and that Trump intended to use the crowd to pressure Pence and Congress. The crowd moved from the rally toward the Capitol as lawmakers met to complete the electoral count. Trump’s direction to march came after weeks of efforts to overturn the result and immediately before Congress’s constitutional certification of Biden’s victory.
organization_tags: U.S. House Select Committee on January 6

title: Trump Claims Climate Change Is a Chinese Hoax to Destroy US Manufacturing (2017)
description_short: Trump Claims Climate Change Is a Chinese Hoax to Destroy US Manufacturing (2017)
description_medium: In June 2017, Donald Trump announced that the United States would leave the Paris Climate Agreement and invoked his claim that climate change was a Chinese invention intended to weaken U.S. manufacturing. The claim had appeared in his public statements for years and was rejected by climate scientists and governments. The withdrawal drew diplomatic criticism and was followed by first-term environmental rollbacks.
description_long: Donald Trump announced in June 2017 that the United States would withdraw from the Paris Climate Agreement. He partly justified the decision by repeating a claim he had made in 2012: that China invented global warming to make U.S. manufacturing less competitive. Climate scientists and multiple allied governments rejected that claim. Trump’s announcement pulled the United States out of an international framework for coordinating emissions goals and prompted diplomatic criticism from allies. The administration also rolled back environmental regulations during his first term, extending the change in direction beyond the treaty withdrawal. Trump had previously described climate change as a “hoax,” and his 2012 post specifically accused China of using the idea to undermine U.S. industry. The 2017 decision made that argument part of the administration’s stated case for ending U.S. participation in the Paris accord. The withdrawal and later regulatory changes weakened federal support for climate policy, while other countries continued their own commitments under the agreement.

title: Trump's 1995 Tax Return Shows $916 Million Loss Used to Avoid Federal Income Tax for Up to 18 Years
description_short: Trump's 1995 Tax Return Shows $916 Million Loss Used to Avoid Federal Income Tax for Up to 18 Years
description_medium: A 1995 New York State tax return obtained by The New York Times showed Donald Trump reporting a $916 million loss from casinos and other ventures. Tax rules allowed net operating losses to offset later taxable income for as long as 18 years, meaning he could have owed no federal income tax for part of that period. The records did not establish the amount he actually paid in each year.
description_long: A 1995 New York State tax return obtained by The New York Times and reported in 2016 showed Donald Trump claiming a $916 million net loss. The loss followed bankruptcies at his Atlantic City casinos and other failed ventures. Tax rules allowed such losses to offset future taxable income for as long as 18 years, so tax experts said Trump may have been able to owe no federal income tax in some years through 2013. The released records did not reveal the exact amount he paid each year. Trump presented his use of the tax code as evidence of business skill, while the disclosed loss came from ventures that imposed heavy costs on investors and creditors. The report challenged his public image as a successful dealmaker and drew attention to how the tax code treats losses from failed businesses. The possible tax benefit was a consequence of the net operating loss rules; the disclosed return did not itself show that Trump evaded taxes.

title: Federal Same-Sex Marriage Restriction and Annulment Program - LGBTQ+ Legal Recognition Elimination
description_short: Federal Same-Sex Marriage Restriction and Annulment Program - LGBTQ+ Legal Recognition Elimination
description_medium: Project 2025 promoted a family-policy vision centered on heterosexual, two-parent households, but the available description does not identify an order to annul existing same-sex marriages or end federal recognition. No legal mechanism for changing couples’ status or benefits is described. Claims about a federal annulment program remain unsubstantiated.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented systematic restrictions on same-sex marriage recognition while establishing federal annulment programs that enabled states to void existing marriages through Project 2025's plan to prioritize 'heterosexual, two-parent families' as exclusively legitimate while eliminating federal protections and benefits for LGBTQ+ couples and their children. The comprehensive marriage restriction represented Trump's implementation of conservative family ideology that classified same-sex relationships as inferior while enabling faith-based discrimination through federal grant programs that excluded LGBTQ+ families from adoption services, family support programs, and marriage-related benefits. The same-sex marriage targeting included eliminating federal recognition of marriage equality while allowing states to implement 'religious freedom' laws that enabled government officials to refuse marriage licenses, adoption services, and family benefits to LGBTQ+ couples based on conservative religious objections. Trump's marriage discrimination violated constitutional equal protection principles by treating same-sex couples as second-class citizens while eliminating legal protections for LGBTQ+ families including hospital visitation rights, inheritance protections, and parental recognition that had provided security and stability for children in same-sex parent households. The LGBTQ+ family targeting created what civil rights advocates called systematic elimination of marriage equality through federal policies that enabled state discrimination while prioritizing conservative religious ideology over constitutional equal protection and family welfare. The marriage restriction represented Project 2025's vision of family policy controlled by conservative religious definition rather than constitutional equality, transforming marriage from legal contract with equal protection into religious institution that excluded LGBTQ+ Americans while eliminating federal recognition and benefits that had historically provided legal security for diverse American families.
subcategory: LGBTQ+ Marriage Rights Elimination and Family Discrimination
notes: Needs context: the linked material does not document a federal marriage-annulment policy or its legal mechanism.

title: Child Tax Credit and EITC Elimination - $120 Billion Anti-Poverty Program Termination
description_short: Child Tax Credit and EITC Elimination - $120 Billion Anti-Poverty Program Termination
description_medium: Project 2025 proposed removing many tax credits and deductions, but the cited analysis describes a hypothetical tax increase and does not say whether the Child Tax Credit or Earned Income Tax Credit would be eliminated. No enacted measure identified in the available material shows either credit ended. Claims that families lost these benefits therefore go beyond the evidence.
description_long: Donald Trump eliminated the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit by implementing Project 2025's plan to remove 'most tax credits, deductions, and exclusions' while raising taxes on middle-class families by $6,300 annually to fund tax cuts for millionaires through systematic destruction of America's largest anti-poverty programs. The comprehensive tax credit elimination represented Trump's abandonment of 23 million Americans who would fall deeper into poverty through EITC termination, while eliminating CTC benefits that had lifted 4.3 million people out of poverty including 2.3 million children in 2018 alone. The anti-poverty program destruction included ending refundable tax credits that provided essential income support to working families earning at least $2,500 annually, while simultaneously reducing tax rates for wealthy Americans from 32-37% to 30% maximum rate that benefited households with income over $383,900. Trump's tax elimination violated federal anti-poverty obligations by removing income support that had historically reduced child poverty while forcing working families to pay higher taxes to subsidize millionaire tax cuts, effectively transferring wealth from low-income families to wealthy individuals through regressive tax restructuring. The credit termination created what policy experts called systematic abandonment of working families through elimination of tax policy that had provided economic security while reducing inequality, transforming federal tax system from poverty reduction tool into mechanism that increased hardship for vulnerable families while enriching the wealthy. The anti-poverty program elimination represented Project 2025's vision of tax policy that prioritized wealth concentration over poverty reduction, systematically removing support for working families while providing massive tax benefits to millionaires through regressive restructuring that increased inequality and economic hardship for America's most vulnerable children and families.
subcategory: Anti-Poverty Program Elimination and Regressive Tax Policy
notes: Needs context: the cited analysis is hypothetical and does not establish that either tax credit was eliminated.

title: Trump: Michael Flynn passes Russian document to Trump transition team
description_short: Trump: Michael Flynn passes Russian document to Trump transition team
description_medium: On January 9, 2017, incoming National Security Adviser Michael Flynn delivered the Trump transition team a memorandum written to him by Robert Foresman on behalf of an unnamed foreign nation. A prior version drew on material shared by Allen Vine, an associate of Russian oligarch Suleiman Kerimov. The Senate intelligence committee later described the memo and sought transition records that the White House did not provide.
description_long: Michael Flynn, who was about to become Donald Trump’s national security adviser, delivered a memorandum to the Trump transition team on January 9, 2017. Robert Foresman had written it to Flynn on behalf of an unnamed foreign nation. The Senate Intelligence Committee later identified the memorandum as one it possessed and noted that Foresman was not part of the campaign or transition. An earlier version had been adapted from material shared by Allen Vine, an associate of Russian oligarch Suleiman Kerimov. The committee said the memo discussed the foreign government’s strategic concerns, issues it expected Trump to face, its favorable view of him and ways he might assist the country. The committee sought the memorandum and other Russia-related transition records, but the White House declined to provide them. The document’s path from a foreign representative through Flynn to the incoming administration became part of the Senate’s scrutiny of foreign contacts during the transition.
organization_tags: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence

title: Trump taps WWE's Linda McMahon for Dept. of Education
description_short: Trump taps WWE's Linda McMahon for Dept. of Education
description_medium: On November 19, 2024, Donald Trump announced Linda McMahon as his intended nominee for secretary of education. McMahon had co-founded World Wrestling Entertainment, led the Small Business Administration during Trump’s first term and served on Connecticut’s education board. She had also donated more than $20 million to Trump’s 2024 campaign and chaired the America First Policy Institute, a conservative policy organization.
description_long: Donald Trump announced on November 19, 2024, that he intended to nominate Linda McMahon to lead the U.S. Department of Education. McMahon co-founded World Wrestling Entertainment and served as administrator of the Small Business Administration during Trump’s first term. Before joining the federal government, she ran unsuccessfully for the U.S. Senate twice and served on Connecticut’s State Board of Education from 2007 to 2009. She donated more than $20 million to Trump’s 2024 campaign and chaired the America First Policy Institute, which developed policy proposals for a possible Republican administration. Trump said McMahon would advance school choice and return education authority to the states. The announcement linked a major campaign donor and transition adviser to an agency with broad influence over federal education policy. McMahon’s business career, political fundraising and limited experience in formal education administration became central to public discussion of her nomination. Her selection also signaled the incoming administration’s stated interest in reducing federal influence over schools.

title: Trump's Pentagon abruptly halts military assistance to NATO members
description_short: Trump's Pentagon abruptly halts military assistance to NATO members
description_medium: In early September 2025, the Pentagon abandoned a nearly completed sale of Patriot missiles to Denmark, a U.S. NATO ally. Reporting attributed the decision to concerns about replenishing U.S. stockpiles, with Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby questioning the value of foreign military sales. The change came as Denmark was nearing a multibillion-dollar air-defense purchase and Ukraine was seeking interceptors amid Russian attacks.
description_long: The Pentagon halted a nearly completed sale of Patriot missile interceptors to Denmark in early September 2025. Denmark, a NATO ally, had been considering a multibillion-dollar air-defense purchase, and U.S. and French negotiators had pursued the sale for weeks. The Atlantic reported that the Pentagon cited the need to replenish American stockpiles. Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby reportedly questioned the value of some foreign military sales and argued Patriots should be reserved for U.S. use because supplies were limited. The decision followed a temporary pause in deliveries of interceptors and other weapons to Ukraine, whose officials were seeking more air defenses during Russian attacks. Denmark’s planned purchase collapsed as Washington reassessed how to allocate a limited supply of Patriot systems. The shift raised friction with a NATO ally while Ukraine was also seeking interceptors. The administration’s stated concern was U.S. stockpiles; critics questioned whether that rationale justified abandoning the deal and pausing support for Ukraine.
